title: Fast Track Sagrada Familia Guided Tour
description: Exploring La Sagrada Familia without a guide means you may miss out on the UNESCO World Heritage Site's hidden details and secret symbols. Make the most of Antoni Gaudí’s masterpiece and beat lines often in excess of three hours on a skip-the-line tour. A choice of entry times allows you to be flexible with your vacation schedule: Opt for the earliest time slot for a less-crowded experience at the Barcelona icon.

reviews.usertext:
This is one off experience and our guide, Raul, made it very enjoyable.

Lots of interesting facts offered and plenty of opportunity to ask questions and take photos. Raul’s English is excellent and he is very clear to understand and has a nice sense of humour.

The building is spectacular inside and out.

We chose to view the other Gaudi buildings we visited from the outside only so as not to add additional expense to our holiday but would recommend paying extra for this guided tour.

Whilst the tour bypasses the singe entry queues, there are is some queuing required to get through security and it’s very busy! You spend about 30 mins of 1.5 hours on queuing/ security and waiting to begin.

My boyfriend and I had a great experience on this tour. I 100% recommend booking a guided tour - you'll learn so much more than meets the eye in this absolutely incredible building.

You are given earphones to hear the guide better (it's a lot of hustle and bustle inside, so it's worth it).

After using a similar service in Seville a few years ago, we wanted to (A) fast track the long que's outside Sagrada Famillia, and (B) have an English speaking guide to understand all the features and ongoing work. Booking was very easy, price seemed good in comparison to similar services, the office opposite was easy to locate, the group was small, and our guide was friendly, relaxed, amusing and very informatitve. We were all issued personal disposable headphones to hear the guides comentary inside the cathedral. Well worth booking this fast track and tour.

Please save your money - we did the ticket via Expedia it was a fast track ticket with tower access and English / French tour. It was through Julia travel. It was so disorganized and such a waste. It was both English and French which made the 45 minute tour majority French. Spent more time waiting in lines and tour started at 9 and we didn’t enter the sagrata until 9:45, and spent about 20 minutes inside just standing still. It was painfully slow, walking about 3 feet and stopping again. You are so much better off getting the audio guide and going yourself. She skipped a lot inside the church and chose to talk a lot about the stones used to construct it. Getting into the tower was another super long wait in line while others without a group go in immediately. Our tour guide was nice but was super slow, disorganized on getting us anywhere, repeated herself a lot and let the French guests push her around. It was a much bigger group than I expected for the cost - about 25/30 people. Only about 7 of the guests were French yet 70% of the tour was in French. Such a waste of money, her actually speaking was about 45 minutes and majority of that was in French. The tower is FANTASTIC. Amazing views and worth the ticket, just a lot of steps down - beware if you take someone not super mobile. The sagrata is amazing I am just frustrated how poor the tour itself was.

Gaudi was amazing and his vision for this cathedral is mind-boggling. Definitely do a guided tour. You most likely must book tickets at least several days in advance. The lighting inside is very much affected by the amount of daylight and also whay time of day. So if you can look at the forecast .. pick the sunniest day and I would recommend either a morning or afternoon tour time.. right at noon I am sure is nice, but the sun being either fully on the east side or fully on the west side makes for quite the light show. The guide did a great job. For those Christians sensitive to breaking the 2nd commandment, this cathedral is one of the easiest to avoid violations (on the inside) the whole outside is a violation, but that is standard catholicism. Nonetheless, this was a beautiful experience. Gaudi's plan to make the supports look like trees was genius.

The tour guide I had for a monolingual English only tour had very broken English with terrible pronunciation. She used incorrect words constantly to try and explain something and it was really a chore to try to understand her. It's OK in a bar or resteraunt but when giving a tour on something so intricate and in depth you really need to talk better English. Me and my wife took our headphones off after 30 minutes because it was impossible to actually understand her. Very disappointing for the cost. Unreal as the official tour is like 20 euros for entry is like 10 euros so we paid 70 euros to basically have a woman speak in a very strong Spanish accent and terrible articulation.

It was not helped by the rain, but it was certainly not feel fast track. To justify the additional cost I think it needs to be slicker and actually faster than the people waiting in the line…
Tour guide was helpful and friendly. Personally I’d opt for mono-lingual if I did it again.

First, the Sagrada is a MUST see! It is absolutely spectacular and worth every penny of your entrance fee...the interior is unbelievable.

We booked this tour for October 2021, the off-season for tourism. Based on the lines at the Sagrada ticket booth, I would have skipped paying extra for this tour. The lines were relatively short and you can do a self-guided tour with earphones. Consider the time of year and day of the week before paying extra for a fast track tour; really wasn't much faster.

The tour itself was frustrating because I thought I booked an English speaking tour. However, Julia Tours decides if you get an English speaking tour OR a bilingual tour and you won't know until you get there. We received the bilingual tour which led to our tour guide giving the tour in both English and Spanish. Based the little bit of Spanish I know, it was obvious on what I could understand and the amount of time our guide spoke in Spanish, the English version of the tour was much more condensed. Our tour guide was very nice and I have no idea if this was intention or not, but it was disappointing.

Confirm before you buy!

We enjoyed the trip to the Sagrada, it was very beautiful and the guide was informative.

HOWEVER, the guide left me and my sister behind in the security line when they were checking our bags and we couldn't find the group. We ended up having to ask a member of staff to tell us where the museum was because my sister remembered the tour guide said they were starting in there. When we finally found the group, the tour guide hadn't even noticed we were missing and we didn't get the audio devices, which presumably everyone else got while we were still in the security line.

Seeing the Sagrada Familia was an amazing experience and definitely should be a must-see for visitors to Barcelona. We are certainly happy that we went to see it and overall the tour wasn't bad.

However, we booked the English Bilingual tour, as that was the only one with availability on the day we were free. This shouldn't have been a problem, but we found that we really didn't a full explanation of what we were seeing / the history of the church. I don't speak great Spanish, but I understand enough that we were only getting about half of the information that was being provided in Spanish. (It was also obvious when the guide would spend 5-7 minutes talking in Spanish and then share only 5-6 sentences in English.)

I feel like our tour guide did the best he could. The management needs to do a better job of screening who takes groups on English (an option) speaking tours. He was kind and knew the facility well. His English was extremely difficult to understand (he is a mumbled).
He walked extremely quickly and there were older people in the group who struggled to keep up.
He lost folks very quickly in the beginning of our tour.
This building was magnificent, so I am certainly disappointed for paying $50 for nothing.

The Sagrada Familia has been under construction for 140 years and has many interesting stories to tell. Our guide was very informative and pointed out things about this amazing cathedral that we would never have known if we had gone on our own. She was very open to questions and let us take time to let it all sink in. We would definitely recommend this tour for anyone who wants to get a good overview of this amazing place.

The fast pass piece was good. We still waiting about 40 min to enter however our tour guide gave us too much info and thus his talking delayed entering the church. Everything took longer as well because he had to repeat things in 2 languages. When we entered the church we stood in the same spot for 20 minutes while he talked. It limited the amount of things we could see and standing in the same spot was uncomfortable

This tour was guided by a very knowledgeable gentleman. Unfortunately we did not catch his name but he was super knowledgeable and very patient with the questions he was receiving. I loved the radio and headphones we were provided upon starting the guide as this tends to be a very busy attraction with lots of people the radio and headphones allowed us to clearly hear our tour guide over all of the noise. This church is spectacular with the architecture and stained glass throughout the church it definitely a must see when in Barcelona.

It wasnt that obvious on the booking confirmation that we had to go somewhere other than the Sagrada to pick up the tour/tickets so we nearly missed the start - make sure you check instructions carefully. The ticket office is close but without Google Maps we would have missed it completely. We had a great tour guide, Marc P who was very knowledgeable and friendly. Tour doesn't last 1.5 hours though, we were finished just after an hour. Would really recommend booking a tour as the queues were awful and standing around in the heat would be unpleasant. Thanks Marc!

Our experience was 1, our tour guide Ava (5pm 15/7/2022)
Her English was so bad we couldn’t understand her fully. She couldn’t properly explain which stone was used for the strongest column. Tried to spell it but we were still confused. The reason for a tour guide is to get an understanding of the history of this amazing building and a insight into the life of Antoni Gaudi and we were completely under whelmed.
Our experience was so bad we are requesting a full refund.
Thank you
Robyn Randall (5 pp)

The tour lasts about an hour to an hour and 20 minutes. If you want to do it in a tour setting I would recommend this method. The Julia Tours that we used started at their store which is across the street from the church.

The actual tour uses a headset that you keep so you can listen to the guide. Although you can do the church by itself and walk around you will certainly not fully understand the construction or what you are looking at without a guide of some sort. I’ve been to many churches and this one is extremely unique. Very impressive. Go at least twice to really get the size of it.

We have done this tour before and the guide was super knowledgeable. This time around it was very disappointing. The guide had very limited knowledge, just the basics that we could have googled and saved our money. Her English was very broken and hard to understand and to top it all off, one of the couples did not speak English so she spent most of the time translating and engaging with them in Spanish, which was the language she felt most comfortable with. Very very disappointing to the point where we wanted our money back.

We are English speakers and were assigned to a Spanish/English guide with about 30 mostly Spanish speakers. The Sagrada Familia is amazing and While our guide tried to speak about all the amazing details...much more was done in Spanish. Her English was hard to understand with our communication devices. We would highly recommend getting a English speaker only and a smaller group...would be worth the difference.

We felt that the advert was misleading as the duration of the visit was marketed as 1 hour and 30 minutes. In reality, the guided tour was 30 minutes in duration. This is not to say that our guide was not knowledgeable or unhelpful, but we would appreciate more transparency from the agency what we are actually paying for and therefore set realistic expectations.

Irina was the perfect guide to help us get the most from this amazing tour. She wove together the history and science of this truly unique and awesome project, which continues to evolve, with ease and enthusiasm. The air conditioned museum with 10 minute video is well worth the time after the official tour is over.
Thank you Irina!

This tour was amazing. We had a great guide who talked through the historic, cultural and religious aspects of La Sagrada Familia. We learned a lot about the details of the facades that I would have never known or noticed without taking this tour. Entry was smooth and streamlined and we got to spend as much time as we wanted inside after the tour was completed. I highly recommend a visit to the towers! The views were incredible and this really highlighted our entire experience.

Though the lines weren’t terribly long to get in, having a bilingual guide made the visit much more informative and interesting. Marc was attentive to the group, moved efficiently through the cathedral, yet took time to answer questions. Having the wireless headsets to hear him was a real bonus. Definitely would recommend.

The tour was fine. It was conducted in both Spanish and English, one right after the other, so a lot of time was wasted hearing the information twice. I would have preferred a little more in-depth information but I guess that is what private tours are for. The tour guide was friendly and knowledgable, and we were given a brief overview of the different elements of the cathedral.. I would personally try a different tour if i had it to do over again.

We really didn't know what to expect. We had just been told that it was must to see. It was breathtaking to see and then again to walk inside. We loved how the host shared so much history and knowledge about the meaning behind every pillar, window, and detail.

This was advertised as 10-20 people, we had 28 in our group, too large of a group. Only as advantage was probably the expedited entrance hat I don’t think was that was that expedited. The tour was so so. I’m not sure an audio tour may nor have been better. I’d research you options for an advance ticket purchase with guaranteed entrance time

The visit itself was excellent. However we arrived a little late and instead of letting us join our group they made us pay an extra 29 euro/pers to change our ticket to a later time slot. And we didn't even get the original ticket that we paid for, which allowed a visit of the towers.

This tour was supposed to be for 1.5 hours but in reality it was about 30 min. We spent the rest of the time waiting for the tour guide and to get in the church. Our guide was very knowledgeable but this tour is NOT worth the money they charge. We were so disappointed and I do NOT recommend this tour!

We booked this tour through our hotel, Alexandra Barcelona. They made it very easy for us.

We arrived at Julia travel at the appointed time and our guide arrived a few minutes later.

We booked an English/multi language tour. An English only would have been more convenient but not sure that option existed.

We were in a group of 7 that ballooned to 12 by the time we arrived at the security screening. Not sure how they all found us but it was apparently. Wry seamless despite a thousand tourists in the immediate area.

Screening was relatively efficient and more detailed than TSA through the airport. They want to look in all bags but not touch or open, that’s your job.

The tour guide Clara was very knowledgeable and thorough. She alternated back and forth between English and Spanish easily. Spanish takes so much more time(words) to say the same thing.

We spent approximately 1.5 hours on the tour. She took us all throughout the Basilica and we completed the tour at the entrance to the museum. We spent an additional 1.5 hrs seeing additional features including the Gaudi museum and taking pictures.

Clara was very nice to everyone and was kind enough to take time to answer questions from well-meaning passersby who mistook her for a docent or representative of La Sagrada or just needed help. Clara is definitely a strength for Julia travel. We would highly recommend her.

I would recommend this tour.

I paid for an guided tour in English and ended up in a group that was both Engligh and French which I didn't appreciate. It made the waiting around much longer than it needed to be... Tour guide was also a bit rude. Overall, not worth the money.

Our guide was terrific with lots of great insights into the basilica’s history
Also, The light thru the stain glass windows was incredibly. An inspirational experience. We attended church services the next morning. This is a must see if in Barcelona

Sara was our tour guide and she was very funny and knowledgeable. Since the Sagrada Familia is still being built, the tour feels kind of short, but honestly, it is enough time and very informative. We had time to go off on our own inside and look around. The tour is very helpful because there are so many small details that would be missed otherwise had they not been pointed out. We did the morning tour so when it was over we were able to explore some more on our own and visit the museum as well. I would highly recommend this tour to anyone.

What an amazing building I was breath taken it was beautiful. It was my first time seeing this building in Barcelona. The only problem I found was being on a tour with a group. The time was very short not enough time to explore the building which means you need to go back to Barcelona and actually stay a few days to enjoy the whole place

This fast track tour of the Sagrada Familia by Julia Tours was very good and enjoyable, with a knowledgable guide and prompt departure. Our guide was friendly and knowledgable but could have been more considerate. It was a blazing hot day, and she had us wait for approximately 10 minutes in the direct sun, more than once. She also did not indicate bathroom locations, nor did she pause for any restroom breaks. When two in our group had to leave to find one, our guide did not stop at all and steamrolled forward, leaving us to scramble to direct our family members who left so they wouldn't get left behind. Although the tour portrayed many great facts and information and allowed us to quickly gain entrance, the tour was shorter and less detailed than the one I had before, and the guide did not show as much passion or admiration in her work, neither was she very considerate to members of our group. Overall, it was a good tour, but it could be much better.

Our guide was friendly and informative. Did not love it though. Told it was a 90 minute tour. As usual started a little late. Had to wait while he got tickets. So our 10:00 tour really started at 10:30 and ended at 11:10. I would advise getting your own tickets and using the audio guide. After the tour we still walked around for a while on our own. The skip the line didn’t seem to help us but maybe April is not super high season yet. No dress code was enforced in any way which was frustrating because I wanted to wear sandals and the description said closed shoes. Saw shorts, tshirts, bare shoulders etc. Very unusual church. Glad I went but loved the Barcelona Cathedral with its rooftop visit more.

The tour was very disorganized at the start. Getting from the Julia Travel office through the mobs to get into Sagrada Familia, It was easily 20 minutes before we were standing inside of security and looking at the church. That's when the tour finally began. 30 people is too many for a tour. It felt very impersonal. Eva was a good tour guide and is passionate about the beauty of Sagrada Familia but the crowds and the pushing and the challenges of staying near our guide made this a far less than wonderful experience. It was difficult to take in and appreciate the beauty of the church. We left the tour about 15-20 minutes before it's end. Dual language tours may work well for Julia Travel but is not good for the customer. I felt like we heard less about the church because Eva had to say everything twice, so we only got 50% of what we might have learned if it had been in a single language. She did her best, I don't fault Eva at all, but she was in an untenable position. Avoid Dual language tours.

The tour was bilingual, which was not prominently advertised when we booked. That is not why we are giving a bad review. The problem was that the guide's English (and Spanish) were difficult to understand. Large portions of the tour were given out in the sun for no reason. For example, to discuss a tiny model of the church. This is not a tour where "stories" are told about the history of Sagrada. Very superficial. "Look at the facade." Would not recommend.

The guide was very good and knowledgeable and spoke good English.

The actual tour did not start until about 2:30pm (booking was for 2pm) as the guide was getting tickets and headphones after we set off. The tour then finished at 3:30pm.

Thought it was overpriced and not good value for money considering it was only for an hour.

We booked audio guide and it was helpful so we could wander round and still hear guide. He spoke several sentences at a time in English or Spanish so it gave us chance to wander round to take photos while he was speaking Spanish. Had a good use of English and good knowledge of the subject. He emphasised Gaudi's vision and spirituality which as Christian's we found very encouraging. Cant wait till the resurrection facade is finished and we will be back again.

The Meet-up point was easy to find and if you get there early, there is a restaurant across the street where you can chill outside and have a beer.

Our tour started on time. I was happy that we were outfitted with wireless communication with earbuds.

Our tour guide provided an excellent overview of what we were able to experience. As a result and we breeze through security.

He explained the reasoning behind the exterior architecture and an excellent overview of Antoni Gaudi.

We walked us through the interior pointing out various areas of interest. Since it was sunny that day, the light shone brightly through the brilliant stained glass.

This is a place that should be on your bucket list. Get the "skip the line" past, it is worth having the excellent narration.

My first bad experience with guided tour and from trip advisor. We booked english guide tour and in the end we had our guide talk first in spanish and then in english looks like they simply want to save time buy mixing two language grups in one... It was confusing at it best. Felt like wasting of our time, especially when every minute or two when you had to wait for guide to translate what she said in other language.

We used Barcelona Bus Tour to get to the location, stops right outside and tour office is 100 meters away. Our tour party was multi lingual so the guide spoke in Spanish and English. He was very knowledgable and made the tour very interesting. You cannot fail to be impressed by the size of this building and the attention to detail. The inside simply took your breath away and the colours coming through the stained glass windows were breathtaking. They say building work will be completed by 2026, 100 years since the death of Guadi, that must be a reason to come back to this wonderful city and re visit this stunning building.

The office was well organized, check in was super easy, guide showed up on time and spoke very good English.

Decided this was the best way to go to see such an amazing basilica as the guide WILL make the difference for understanding more about the history. Group wasn’t overly big, maybe 15 - 17 and headsets are used so you can wonder a bit and take photos and still here your guide.

We are very happy we did the 4 pm tour ! Sophia (I think?) was our guide and gave us a lot of info about the symbolism and history behind this unique and beautiful church We started promptly and her English was excellent ! Answered many questions from us. Only complaint was that it was an English speaking tour but there was one Spanish speaking couple with the group of 10ish. So the tour took twice as long as expected because Sophia had to do everything in both languages. That wasn't her fault and she handled it like a champ. We were lucky to be there in late afternoon with the sun going down - the stain glass windows are gorgeous and even more-so with the sun coming through them.

The tour guide Xavier was so knowledgeable I didn’t want it to end, and I’m usually someone who ditches the tour guide once inside. He had so many details it was really game changing.
On the admin side I did see a young couple with an infant have a harrowing experience because they weren’t allowed to take their infant on the tour but couldn’t pay for the tour? It took quite a while of the behind the desk staff to become understanding and solve the problem.

Very hot mid day and most of the tour is outdoors looking at the facade so schedule early. 2 pm was grueling heat.

Sarah was an excellent tour guide. She was knowledgable, patient, and funny. She shared so many interesting details that would have gone either unnoticed or misunderstood, while leaving enough time to attain photographs of each section of the cathedral. Don't worry about needing to be close to the guide to hear the details, all can be heard from a tiny headset. :-)

The Sagrada Familia was even more beautiful than it was crowded. This is a must see, especially with a guide. Unless you have done research on this place you will not understand any of the architectural choices and symbolism. I would suggest taking time after the tour to browse the museum and Gaudi's crypt. Well worth the time and energy.

Well, the Sagrada Familia is amazing and you can't miss it. It's interesting to learn all about Gaudi and different features of the cathedral. But do you need a guide who talks as if it's a recorded audio-guide? Just get the audio-guide, at least you can fast forward. She talked quickly and in a monotone, taking no questions and did not seem to have a sense of humor. It was not fun or relaxing.

Great tour of the cathedral courtesy of our guide Irina! Head sets were an excellent idea so we didn’t miss anything even when lost sight of her! Definitely a good idea to get there early before the crowds. It was lovely just to sit and absorb the atmosphere. Museum underneath was interesting especially the photos showing the stages the cathedral was built in. Really do hope they finish it as a tribute to Gaudi. Totally recommend going.
La sagrada familia itself was incredible. Our guide was fine. I’m sure it’s difficult to wrangle a group of 40-50 in a busy area. The listening devices were nice so that we could all hear her.

Very well organized tour. No waiting in any lines. Ran smoothly and on time. Our guide was great. I would have appreciated more history, architecture, and art perspective in the content of the tour. There was some of that but the guide also spent a lot of time describing the religious meaning of sculptures. I am not religious, so this was less interesting to me.

This tour company and its operators are horrible. I was exposed to COVID and after informing them, they still refused to change my date. Trying to be reasonable with them was impossible. They kept transferring my calls and giving me other numbers or telling me to go find a hospital despite the fact I'm feeling sick and exhausted for their verification. FURTHERMORE, they said my verification would only count for my ticket alone and NOT my partner's. They apparently wanted us to go on separate days and didn't understand he was probably exposed too.

I don't even know who to complain to if this is the type of customer service they provide.

You really can't be prepared for what you are about to see. From a distance the Sagrada Familia looks tall and pretty impressive. When you're on site you really understand what an amazing structure that it is. The sheer height of the domed ceiling and the light coming through the stained glass windows on a sunny day is amazing. I can't stress the importance of having a knowledgable guide rather than "going it alone". The guide that we had on the day, Clara, was fantastic. Wouldn't hesitate to recommend this to anybody.

Our tour was both in English and in Spanish and she did an amazing job. Because she spoke a sentence in English then the same sentence in Spanish, we were able to refresh our language skills! The headsets were a life saver and kept us from having to rush to be near our guide constantly. We could rest assured that we wouldn’t miss a single word if people got between us. The Segrada Familia was breathtaking! Her knowledge of the history was fantastic and flowed well from stop to stop.

We did not tour the towers because there is no elevator down, only up. Didn’t want to walk 400 steps back down. After the tour, we were able to take our time and go through the museum, back around the inside and were not rushed out. It was a wonderful tour and was particularly moving to see the Bible depicted in images. Gaudi was a genius.

We got in ahead of the long lines so that was great. The church is incredibly beautiful so it’ll be a grand experience, with or without a guide. There were 11 people in our group although it says they don’t have anymore than 9. I felt that it was too expensive for the general information we received from the guide. An audio tour would’ve been much better. Basically, you’re paying a lot of money to cut through the lines. If you have the time, I recommend you do this on your own.

Sagrada Familia is a miracle that have to be seen to feel the spirit of this place. There is not a detail that is without reason here. This is not just a church, this is an unique place. In the Sagrada Familia, art, religion, the spiritual and nature are intertwined. Highly recommend to visit this fantastic building. Most probably this is the most visited church in the world.

The guided tour was excellent and very informative. Skip the line tickets made entry fast and easy. The only unfortunate part was that our group doubled in size part way through the tour which made it more difficult to maneuver through the basilica.

Excellent guide, Raul was outstanding and very knowledgeable about everything, we could feel his passion for what he does. He was great and he deserves 5 stars!
On the contrary, a bilingual tour is a completely waste of time, moreover for tourists who might be under a tight agenda. We’ve done Spanish-English and the tour lasted 90 minutes when this could have been no more than 40. My recommendation: do not hire a double language tour and seek for another option (there are many companies doing the same tours) but if you want a passionate guide like Raul, this guise totally makes the difference!

This place is worth seeing in a lifetime, and if you got your tour guide IRINA, count yourself lucky. Irina was a very professional tour guide, expand every detail and got an amazing sense of humour.
Ирина спасибо Вам большое за тур.

Well worth paying for the tour as our guide explained in great detail all the areas in the church and what they stood for. She was extremely informative. The church is amazing and has to be seen from the inside as much as the outside. It looks very different inside as the stained glass windows cannot be seen from the outside and the inside architecture is very different to outside. Well worth a visit.

Sadly we did not complete our tour because we simply just could not hear very well. Although we were provided with whisper clips our guide was very hard to hear. I appreciate this was a bilingual tour but the tour guides English was very hard to understand. It is a shame as we feel we got to visually enjoy the tour but I really wanted to know about the history of the Sagrada Familia. We spoke with another family who had the same difficulties. Such a shame that I have to give this tour a poor rating. :(

You have to see this cathedral to believe it. Under construction for 137 years and will not be complete until 2026 but still something to behold. The tour operator was very knowledgeable and explained much of the details regarding the construction and to explain each thing that we were seeing.

The tour was confirmed the night before but then randomly cancelled the day of less than two hours before the start time. I did not see the email and as a result we were turned away after arriving at the start time. No alternative options were provided. We wound up doing the self-guided tour and it was great. Would stay away from this tour operator.

This tour was an excellent way to see the Sagrada Família. It was my first time visiting Barcelona and it was the first place I wanted to see. We had a knowledgeable tour guide and the headphones made it easy to hear him even when there were lots of people around. We didn’t have to wait in line for tickets and you could stay inside as long as you’d like after the tour to explore on your own. I would definitely recommend it!

Friendly guide and easy check in process. Avoiding the ticket line was worth the price. Group was too big. Audio equipment should be passed out immediately and used outside. We missed much of the talk due to street noise/other groups. Our guide could have told us if the other area to visit in the church and the museum/gift shop below. I would have liked to see the tomb, which was never mentioned.

We enjoyed a great 4pm tour with Clara, our tourguide. She walked us through the Sagrada Familia grounds and Basilica and explained everything so clearly. She had lots of good information and we enjoyed our 90 minutes with her and our small group of tourists. I highly recommend this tour!

Tour pointed out things I didn't know and wouldn't notice on my own. It was good to take, even though it was a little hard to hear every word due to guide's accent and background noise. Just a beautiful interior space and the view from the Tower was worth it. Did the Passion side, since the Nativity was booked up

Our tour guide was Marc, who was knowledgeable and spoke excellent English. Everywhere was extremely busy as you would expect, and it took some time to get in through security and headsets arranged. But the tour delivered and I would recommend it.
The inspired architecture evoking a forest. The use of animals and the natural world in a sacred space. Our guide Marc handled the group with facts, stories, and good cheer. Highly recommended

Fantastic tour guide Raoul took us on a journey through history at the Sagrada Familia, and enticed us with the promise of what’s to come here at this evolving monument of architectural and cultural excellence. At the risk of spoiling everything I’ll just say I hope you like Gaudi! Because we certainly did. Easily recommended.

This tour was wonderful in every way. The company provided a detailed map showing the meeting location, which is directly adjacent to the Church and very convenient. The staff in the office spoke very good English and the tour was punctual. Our tour guide Marc was very knowledgable about Sagrada Familia, answered our questions, and made sure no one got lost. All in all great experience! Highly recommend this company and this location. The only recommendation I would make is for the tour guides to use green laser pointers (for exterior facades), as they are currently using paper in a document sleeve, which is hard to see in the direct sunlight in mid-morning or afternoon.

I think it was a tour that was very well done by our tour guide, Sylvia. There is a a lot to know in terms of the background story involving this amazing piece of architecture. The tour was efficient and done in a very timely manner. They hand out ear pieces like most tours in the area. If you’re ok in spending a little more to get a deeper experience at the sagrada familia, I would definitely recommend this agency.

Irons was amazing! I highly recommend it her! She did a fantastic job! She was very passionate and informative . Dress code was incorrect. No long pants needed.. No need for close toed shoes or long pants or your shoulders we're having your shoulders covered. Love the tour Irina was fantastic!!

We picked this tour because it advertised “sail past the long lines…”
We crept along in the hot sun for almost 30 minutes.
The guide was difficult to understand, and she did not quit talking.
We left the tour and explored on our own.

Gentleman was very informative. This is a must see while here. Once the tour is complete you'll be free to roam around to your liking. I do recommend purchasing the tower tour as well. We didn't get a chance to take it because we realized it was an option after the fact. But the tour in itself cuts the waiting time to get in. Location to pickup the tickets and meet the guide is literally across the street. In all, I highly recommend this package.

Getting into the venue without waiting in long lines was great since my time in Barcelona was limited. Tour was conducted entirely in the requested language. Meeting spot at the tour offices near the venue was convenient. After formal tour was completed, free access to see other venue attractions outside the main sanctuary. Hoped the venue wouldn't be too crowded for 10:00 a.m. tour but ...

SCAM. They never showed up. I asked the people at the café next door to their office and looks like they have been scamming people for months. They sold me tickets to a tour of a place that was closed due to covid. They also never answered emails or picked up the phone. Ever.

Our guide was knowledgeable and friendly. However, thanks s was an English speaking tour and his accent made understanding difficult at times. This was advertised as bypassing the wait in line, but we still had to wait for a while since the guide had to check in and get the radios for the tour. Then we still had to go trough the security scanning which took a while. In all it was probably a good half hour before we actually got inside the cathedral.

The Sagrada Familia is an absolutely stunning church! It was nice to skip the line and moved through the group lines. Our guide Christina, although full of knowledge - her accent was very difficult to understand. Yes, her English was proper but she had a very heavy accent when speaking and it was very distracting to really understand her. My mother who was with me - was very disappointed as she would have liked to understand more about Gaudi and the church but with Christina's very heavy accent - she only understood about half of the information. For older clients or clients who have trouble with accents, this is not a guide to use for English only tours. It made it very disappointing.
We did hear a lot about the

Superb tour. Our guide was fantastic. Full of interesting knowledge, occasional opinions and jokes, and answered any question thrown at him. Segrada Familia was without doubt the most beautiful architecture I have ever seen. Of course it is more than that: it is a sacred place; it is the ongoing work of many to continue the vision of a long dead genius; it is staggering in diversity; it is completely unique. All of those things make it a place that you have to visit, and I recommend this tour if you choose to do that.

We had an English/ Spanish tour of the building. We wish we had taken an English only tour as we felt like we only got half of the information we could have. Also towards the end of the tour, the guide’s English was barely understandable.

I was so happy I booked this tour. We were only in Barcelona for 24 hours and I appreciated that they offered a "Fast Track" option. They were right on time, efficient and provided a great tour of the Sagrada Familia. I was surprised and very impressed with the Basilica and it is a "must see" when you visit Barcelona. It really is incredible.

The tour was in both Spanish and English with the talk provided by the tour guide. He provided details about the structure. The basilica is very impressive and beautiful and well worth a visit. It was nice to be able to get in with very little waiting.

We had a tour through the magnificent Basilica of La Sagrada Famila and Marc P. was our tour guide. He was sooo amazing, very knowledgeable, personable and answered all our questions. I would definitely recommend him as your tour guide. Please look him up when you’re in Barcelona!

The tour was impossibile hear, although it was an english tour, the vast majority of time was devote to a couple of spanish speaking guest. Left the tour, to explore on our own. Loved the church and the museum.

I went on the tour yesterday and was blown away by the beauty of it. The guide was essential to my experience because it allowed me to understand the meanings behind the many details. It was a beautiful building that I will be returning to again. Without the guide I definitely would not have understood the magnitude of detail behind it. Pictures are not enough, you must see it in person!

Breathtaking, Magnifique and Out of this World!

La sagrada familia just sets apart from anything I have ever seen before. Clara, our tour guide, was awesome. Very knowledgeable and attentive.

One day isn’t enough to see every detail.

Excellent guided tour. Well worth getting a fast track ticket to avoid long waiting line. The tour guide Mark (did not get his last name) was knowledgeable and courteous. Marc pointed out important facts and details of the stunning architecture.

Wonderful! La Sagrada Familia is the #1 don't miss place in Barcelona. Get a good guide like this one and go. Take your time and take lots of photos. Everything is symbolic. The genius of the "architect of light" shines here.

Good tour with good information. I signed up for English only but it ended up being bilingual which was a little less pleasant for a 1 hour tour. Felt like we got half of the information because it took time for the translations. When you sign up for an “English only” but don’t get one, you have an expectation that was not met.

Nice place to visit and see the 19 th century beautiful architecture. The place is surrounded by excellent resturants, gardens , shopping for gifts. Anyone visiting Barcelona should pass on Segrada familia

Great tour. Our guide was very knowledgeable and he shared a lot of interesting information. The tour went at a good pace. The directions to meet the tour were not easy to follow -- we weren't the only ones scrambling to find the office. It would have been helpful to give the name of the office and the cross-streets of the corner.

We had Clara as our guide, she was wonderful. It was a bilingual tour which was great for me (I speak English) and for my son who is bilingual! There was so much information that would not be the same if you just walked around on your own! If was a great day and I highly recommend this guided trip to anyone.
The only thing I will point out is that you need to meet at Julia Travel which is on the corner across from the metro. We were a little confused by the directions, but still got there in time!
Great one hour with Irina. I was blown away with the immense structures, artistry and pure genius of the Sagrada Familia. Irina brought the history and significance live with beautiful story telling.

The fast track was not fast track - we waited outside for half an hour. The guide then rushed through everything. Felt like the audio guide would have given more details. So didn’t see the point of paying for a fast track guided tour as both aspects were poor.

Not that good. I presented your confirmation for my tour but the tour company did not have it in their system and the tour was sold out. Did have an opening for a tour two hours later which was fine. Could have been a disaster. Only purpose of one trip to Barcelona was to take this tour.

Purchased a hop on hop off and used it as transportation to Sagrada Familia. Unfortunately they had a shift change which delayed us and we did not make it at the scheduled time for our 3pm tour. We tried to get an exchange at the Julia Travel office of some sort but were told it was not possible. Make sure you take a taxi and make sure you’re there early. Once there we were pointed in at least 3 different directions. It’s a mad house. Very disappointed to have missed it.

Initially found guide difficult to understand. Whisper audio system made it better. Appreciated fast access. Irina very pleasant & knowledgeable. A laser pointer would help highlight areas she's referring to on the exterior. Had a better "exterior" experience with less distraction with our guide on Runnerbean free Gaudi tour.

The tour was good and the guide tried to be funny (which didn't always work out).
He gave a good overview on the different sights to be seen at the Sagrada Familia.
Yes, there was queuing at the beginning, but it was not too much and therefore good to deal with.
However, next time I would buy a normal ticket and also try to get on the tower by lift, which wasn't included for the tour (I suppose because there wouldn't have been enough time).

The Sangra Familia is beautiful and different. Our tour guide was haphazard, did not connect with us at all at the start. We were all talking to each o other to make sure we were following the right lady. She gave decent information, but would not recommend as a tour guide.

I did not know what to expect... my first visit to Barcelona. Gabby met me at Hotel Gallery and we walked to train station ... I thought it would be bus ride with a group! NO The ride was a fantastic experience so I can now navigate BCN trains like a pro! We walked/talked in Montserrat. I got an education! Gabby loves what she does and it shows:)
I will be back! and.. I will recommend my clients .. and I will ask to meet with her again!

Not helpful. Was unable to make my excursion due to a flight cancelation. Contacted the company several times with no response. They finally responded after the tour happened asking for more money in order to reschedule a tour. Disappointed

Marc P. was amazing! We got a private tour because no one else registered for that day and time. Super knowledgeable and so friendly! He took his time with us and answered all of our questions. You definitely want a tour guide for this attraction.
Marc was a great tour guide and knew so many interesting facts about La Sagrada Familia. The tour was very thorough and allowed more time to explore on your own. It was well worth it.

Our tour guide, Donatello, was horrible! She was extra rude to a guest yelling at her over the radio for all to hear and even said, I am being kind to you only because you are a guest. but she was NOT kind at all!! She waisted so much time!!! 35 minutes in and we only were 5 steps inside by the architect timeline. I want my money back!

Loved our tour guide Feliciano-he was very knowledgeable and fun! The food was just ok-loved trying new things but 3 out of 4 were fish and bread of some kind (anchovies/sardines/mackerel). Would have rather had more of a variety. Tip-most of the food came at last place so pace yourself.

Olga was the best guide. Really educated us on the Sagrata Familia. Was very personable and connected with our family well. She mad the tour as good as it was. Without her, I don't think that we would've had the great time that we did. She gave us recommendations on restaurants in the area which was really nice of her. Got to know us on a personal level by simply talking to us and it was very enjoyable getting to know her. I would give her 100 out of 10if I could. The best tour guide I've ever had.

A very good tour. Definitely made seeing Sagrada Familia easier as we didn't have to wait in line for tickets. Security is very tight and we briefly waited in line to get through that. Our guide was knowledgeable and friendly. I would recommend.

Our guide was knowledgeable and professional. The tour was on time and meeting point was near Sagrada Familia. Amazing and magnificent architecture. The Passion tower visit was really worthy. High recommendation.

Very knowledgeable guide who had details about this wonderful church that we had not previously heard. Meeting location is across the street from the Sagrada Familia so very convenient. We have used this tour group previously and would use them again. Recommend.

Office very easy to find. Guide had great info and shared knowledge easily. Pointed out many of the hidden symbolic elements of the church and they are everywhere! Very interesting for a first time visitor!

The breathtaking experience of visiting the basilica was made even better by this tour. Clara, our guide, provided us with fundamental history and architectural explanation. Most importantly, she had a passion for what she shared. Truly a spiritual experience we will never forget. Thank you, Clara! Thank you, Barcelona!

The Basilica is one of the top 5 places I have ever seen in my life. Do whatever it takes to go see it - it’s unbelievable and pictures don’t do it justice.

The tour guide was ok, but definitely do fast track tickets even without a guide.

BEWARE: I am a frequent contributor to Trip Advisor, sharing my experiences for the benefits of other travelers. Normally, I submit complimentary reviews. This is not one of them.

My wife & I were visiting Barcelona for the first time. Based on the glowing reviews posted on Trip Advisor for this particular service of Julia Travel, we acquired tickets for the guided tour of Sagrada Familia. BE ADVISED: based upon our unfortunate experience, you may want to consider another option for your tour of Sagrada Familia.

First, the good: The Sagrada Familia architecture is simply amazing. It is clear Gaudi was a master and his genius is demonstrated in this brilliant basilica.

Unfortunately, we were only able to view it from the outside on the surrounding sidewalk. This after paying 78 Euros in advance to Julia Travel for a guided walking tour inside the basilica. The is due to the fact that we missed the 1200 hours starting time of the tour -- due to our mistake in taking the Metro in the wrong direction, which caused us to arrive at Sagrada Familia @ 1150. This was no doubt our responsibility.

The bad: Julia Travel is very difficult to find. Even when asking for help at Sagrada Familia, people guided us in the opposite direction. It took more than 20 minutes to finally be given the proper direction (after stopping to ask four different times, as they are not marked well on Google maps).

Once we arrived, our tour group had left. The young woman at reception explained that they could not refund us the cost of Sagrada Familia admission (38 Euros for two persons) because they had to pay for the tickets in advance of the tour. However, when we asked that the difference of 40 Euros be refunded to us (as we did not experience the tour of Julia Travel whatsoever), she dismissed us as being 30 minutes late for the scheduled tour departure. She did offer a later tour (which our scheduled could not accommodate) but stated we would have to buy tickets again for that later tour. Bottom-line: we paid 78 Euros and received nothing for the money spent.

The ugly: to add insult to injury, when I plainly expressed my frustration and asked why we were receiving nothing for the 78 Euros, she dismissed us and said "Bye" waving us out the door with the back of her hand. Clearly, her attitude was atrocious as she was rude and disrespectful.

Note: Based upon our experience, I expect Julia Travel to respond to this post, possibly further attempting to place the blame on us -- versus practicing good customer service and, at a minimum, refunding us the 40 Euros for their guided tour service which we did not receive.

In summary, I am not recommending you avoid Julia Travel. I am, however, suggesting you think twice before utilizing their services.

I took this tour with my 16 year old sister this morning. I initially chose to take the tour because I didn't want to navigate lines and crowds at Sagrada Familia. The crowds were tame at 9:00 this morning, but I'm still glad I chose to "skip the line" and go with a group.

Sagrada Familia is beautiful, outside and in! The stained glass windows are awesome on the inside and the scenes on the outside are detailed. Our guide was nice, spoke English well, was informative and seemed to know everything there is to know about the building! However, the tour was a bit boring and didn't offer too much that a pamphlet/book couldn't. We were able to look around the building on our own after the tour was over, which I enjoyed.

I was happy to skip the line, the tour company is professional, but I wouldn't take the tour again. Beware, there are more than one "Julia Travel" meeting points in Barcelona! Make sure you have the right one!

Basilica was spectacular not to be missed.
1) Tour operator company not good. Meeting place was their office near the Basilica. One bathroom for every tour leaving from this location. Not nearly enough to accommodate all the groups.
2) Guide’s English was so heavily accented we understood 1 out of every 5 words and the head sets broke in and out.
3) it was very crowded in the church - the guide would begin talking and pointing out sights before the group was able to crowd in. Missed SO much.
4) Guide held up a small navy blue umbrella for tour group to try to follow through the crowds. Impossible.

Pick a different tour company.

My husband and I took a guided tour of La Sagrada Familia with Julia Tours. An amazing place to visit. The tour was well structured but the guide was covering English and Spanish and it got difficult to follow after a while. Still a must site to visit while in Barcelona!

Julia Travel advertised an English only 90 minute tour but it was only an hour. The tour guide ALEX spoke very poor English and was very difficult to understand. Participants in the tour asked him to speak more slowly but he didn't. Basically he took us in one door of the cathedral and out another door. He also did not take us through the museum and told us to go on our own. We went to the museum and had to listened to a guide leading a tour from another company. Julia Travel representatives were VERY rude to us when we asked for partial reimbursement. Save money and buy tickets directly from the Sagrada Familia website with a headset. You'll get a much better tour!

Meeting point easy to find and only 1 minute walk to Sagrada F. Guide walked us over at start of tour but then we had to wait outside for 40mins until guide got the tickets... Not fast track at all... Then had to wait in line for other groups to go in first... Not good. Guided tour lasted less than 50mins and not the 1:30 expected. Guide was quite knowledgeable but said he had to cut it short due to wait for tickets.... Enjoyed the visit but a tad disappointed with the long wait at the start.

We took the Sagrada skip the line tour yesterday. We did skip the line as advertised but I’m not convinced there was much of a line to skip. Seems that if you pre-purchase your tickets, you’ll get in at the designated time. The tour guide we had from Julia tours, which I gather is the local operator contracted by Viator who we booked through, was mediocre. He was difficult to understand even though we had booked the English only tour. I think having a tour guide for the Sagrada is worthwhile but we were very disappointed with the quality of the tour. The Sagrada itself is exceptional and not to be missed.

It was worth the price to skip the lines but the guide did not give us enough information about the Basilica. He pretty much just walked us around without telling us much about what we were seeing. I learned more doing my own research.

The Cathedral was amazing inside, and the tour guide was obviously knowledgeable.

However, we didn't realise that we had go collect the tickets from the office first. We were first sent to the old address, then got lost trying to find the new address. Despite getting to the cathedral early, we ended up being 15mins late and having to buy a new €19 ticket for the next tour. So read the information carefully and find the office ahead of schedule if you can!

First, it's difficult to find Julia Travel! Directions are just awful, our cabby dropped us off at the taxi area in front of Sagrada while Julia travel is across the park on the other side (found it after asking a few other guides where it was). Next, it is near the Sagrada but the area around the Church is a mad house. The office staff could use a customer service lesson! It was too far to walk from our hotel so a round trip taxi was 12 Euro each way from Las Ramblas. Next, our guide Ignacio was nice but hard to understand. There were tours everywhere jockeying for position and some of the earbuds interfered with others and we heard a screaming baby for a large portion of the beginning. It doesn't seem to matter the time of day (our tour at 10am) was just as crowded as later tours and the only advantage is the skip the line part. The church is gorgeous of course but I would have liked more info for my money. We turned our earbuds in early and walked around alone for a while.

Our tour was disorganized and the tour guide lacking in command of English (this was an English language tour). Much time was spent on exterior points of view and lengthy historical ramblings. The interior tour was limited and rushed.

We were impressed with the architecture but disappointed with the tour and guide.

Well...I would hate to see what the not fast track version would be! We still waited about 30 min to get in (yes...it is Summer, and lots of people trying to get in). The tour was good...lots of information given. If you are an architect or into math, you would love it because the guide was very detail oriented! I am an artist, and zoned out a bit...so a self guided tour might have been best for me:)...

Our wait was not that bad, once we figured out who our tour guide was. I also had to pay my guide extra (which was written on the description, but I didn't see) for the actual tour. But I paid, and we had a great time.

Did this tour earlier in the week. I just read the description above 'sail past long lines of tourists' and had to chucke...We did LOTS of standing around in the sun while the tour guide was texting or talking to her phone and trying to connect with people that were supposed to be in the group or were late or who knows what... we got to the entrance and she said she would go in and get our tickets in 3 minutes... it took more than 10 minutes while we stood out in the sun. The fast track group area were camps of groups and more standing around. Once we got inside her microphone wasn't working and she had to go back several times which meant more standing around. Overall she knew a lot about the Sagrada, Guidi etc and had a good sense of humour. The office where you line up and pick up your ticket (a sticker) is like a sauna... just more hot, stuffy and disgusting. Luckily they said come back 5 minutes before the tour starts to meet the group because I needed some fresh air really badly. The Sagrada itself is impressive beyond words. The amount of time spent on the guided tour of the little school was a bit much by the end of it. Next time though I would rather do a self-guided tour.

The lines at Sagrada Familia can be very long, so investing in a prepaid tour that skips the line is clearly worth the price. The meeting place (Julia Travel) is close to Sagrada Famila and our guide was very knowledgeable about the scriptural bases for much of the statuary and other art. The inside of the church is breathtaking.

Booked this tour online before going on Holiday in Barcelona. We were excited about our trip and visiting Gaudi’s Sagrada Família.

Our tour was at 3pm. We arrived to the office across the street per the instructions upon completion of booking. The office was chaotic, multiple groups waiting. My check in was easy And I was given the 4 tickets for my partner and couple we are traveling with. We waited 15 minutes for our tour guide to call our group.

The groups are about 15 to 20 people. Beware as some people may be older and move very slow so patience is a must. We were given an audio device - by our guide - the audio does is not very clear but worked.

Our tour guide was Jaime and he is great! very knowledgeable and by no means does this review reflect him- once again kudos to Jaime!he is professional and articulate.

We head over to the site and waited another 20 minutes just get in. At this point it’s 3:40 and we are sitting on the curb waiting to enter.

You will go through a security screening much like the airport which was no surprise to me but it was at this point I asked Jaime our guide about the length of the tour and tower access. The tour is 1.5 hour in total and he said only 2 tours have tower access and my tour did not include it. That was disappointing and I felt like the advertising was misleading. So use caution when booking and verify that your tower has tower access if that is of interest to you.

You definitely skip the line but our tour did not start until 45 - 50 minutes after our 3pm expected start time.

Since we had other things booked we ended up giving the audio devices back to Jaime once we were inside and explored the sight on our own.

Overall it was just okay- since we had no tower access we may have been better just going on our own and waiting in line.

Definitely worth seeing! It’s a must see when in Barcelona!
The audio guide for this was worth the extra money and now the kids wish to return in 2026 when it should be finished. The building is beyond words and really is a must do.

We were flying to Barcelona so that my son who has a photography project for school, could take pictures of the Sagrada Familia. We flew in from NYC bought on off bus tickets and waiting until our tour time at 4 pm. We went to the meeting place at 3:45 and they told us it was cancelled and Trip Advisor should have contacted us about the cancellation. Not a word from Trip Advisor and not a refund even at the is point. We wasted 16 hours in an airplane to do this. Unacceptable and we will never book with Trip Advisor again. Their name states Trip Advisor but they did not advise us of anything.

Bought these tickets so I could skip the line, but I was blown away by the tour guide and amount of information I learned! Frankly it is not worth seeing this amazing landmark without a tour, because learning the context on the background of the design, Gaudi's inspiration and planning process, and small details that I wouldn't have noticed on my own made the experience unforgettable. Visit the Sagrada Familia, and visit on a tour!

Went on this tour on July 24, 2018. A lovely tour, and our tour guide (Anna) was a Barcelona native who clearly loved giving tours. She presented a host of anecdotes and nuances about this absolutely stunning church. She knew about a lot about the design with regards to form and function. She understood and conveyed details about artistic choices of Gaudi, and even mentioned other contributors to its design over the last 140 years. I also want to mention, I went on this tour at 3 PM. Anna mentioned that it's her favorite time of day to see the inside of this church, and I've included a picture to show you why. The way the light comes into the church illuminates the stained glass windows in a way that each corner of the place is bathed in red, blue, green or yellow light, which Anna confided is a tribute to the seasons. Just one of the beautiful details that she shared.

I had arrived at the church on the day prior at 12:30pm, and they were no longer allowing visitors for the day. This tour not only eliminates the waiting in line only to find out that they've decided that they've reached their quota of tourists, but gives you a description of everything you're looking at and the ability to ask additional information.

We were a group of 8, and I coordinated advance tickets. Eventually I discovered the Sagrada Famila official website where I purchased tour tickets, they are all timed by the way, and it only cost us 18 euro per person (Dec 2017). Just make sure the date and time are correct. We purchased tickets from our hotel for one of the Parks, and unfortunately showed up the wrong day, and were neither allowed in the park nor issued a refund, but that is another story.

What is to say, very impressive. The church will now be finished in 9 years since they have now started a dedicated fund raiser. The different facades are meant to be viewed from different directions, and the interior is just as impressive with the greenish and reddish stained windows, the natural tree-like columns. Everything is natural, or not artifical, no straight lines, no vertical columns, after all trees don't grow absolutely vertical, and are not perfectly round. Take your time after the guided tour, and just immerse yourself into this very unique experience.

Get there early, and follow the signs to the official entrance where your official tour guide will meet you at the designated time.

We booked the English "Skip the line" 4pm Viator tour of Sagrada Familia. On the plus side; we did skip the line. For $80 for the two of us I expected more; our group was large; maybe 20 people. The tour guide, while peppy, had very accented English and was hard to understand, even with earbuds in our ears channeling her directly into our heads. The Julia Tour office was almost impossible to find; our cabby couldn't understand the directions and neither could we. If you find the dog park in the park in front of the church, the office is directly across the street from the dog park. The church is mad crowded, so once you get in, you are surging thru tons of people. We were recommended to get there after 1pm to see the windows in the best light. They were gorgeous at 4. Of course you have to go see this church, but it was not the highlight of our trip to Barcelona.

The place to see is amazing, and it is an experience definitely enhanced by having a guide give the history and explain what we were looking at, and point out what we should pay attention to. It was also nice when we got in that there were headphones we could use to easily hear our guide Fernando, who was quite good.

Easy to book. The guide was very friendly and made the tour enjoyable.
Getting in was fast and allowed us to enjoy the whole experience.

The Sagrada Familia is one of the few places where no picture can do it justice. Visiting is a spiritual experience. We were fortunate to go when the sun was shining brightly, meaning the cathedral was showered in the stained glass. Our tour guide was excellent, providing history of the Cathedral and discussing the architecture. Make sure to book your appointment early as you don’t want to miss out.

Vinces was a fantastic tour guide. He showed us all the important parts of the chapel, was very knowledgeable and had us all Laughing at his jokes. He also made sure we knew the best places to take pictures. 5 stars!

We used the company Julia T to book a "fast track" guided tour and unfortunately, the day we went, it was pouring rain. Our group stood out in the rain waiting to get into the church for at least 20 minutes. The tour was supposed to start at 11am, but we didn't get in until close to 11:30am. Then when we were finally able to get in, the church office would not agree to provide us with the headphones due to the heavy rain. The result was it was more difficult to hear our guide and we missed a lot of information on the Sagrada. As we were so late in starting, our tour was relatively short - barely an hour when we were expecting more like 1 1/2 hours. The guide was very nice and informative, but this was not worth the money we spent.

We had a terrible experience with Julia Travel for the Sagrada Familia tour. My husband enjoyed the tour whereas I did not appreciate the fanaticism of the guide. Finding the office to check in was incredibly difficult not knowing the area, which caused us to be late. They had us go to meet the tour, but we would have had to wait nearly two hours at the entry gate. We opted instead to rebook for the next day - at a very exorbitant fee. I feel they should have given us directions to the meeting point/their office as well as warned us to arrive up to an hour before the start of the tour to complete check in - since the tour seems to start earlier than advertised.

The tour felt short and like it cherry picked details (of which there are SO MANY) that were of interest to the guide rather than letting us ask questions or asking what anyone in the group wanted to hear/learn. The tour also was just the 'museum' and main body of the cathedral. If you are looking to do a tour of the towers you'll need to book a separate tour or book a combined tour with another company.

We visited here at 11:00 am. Once booked you collect your tickets from the small travel agent shop across the street (at the back of the cathedral to the right hand side ). The tour guide collects you from here. There is a waiting time both for the tour guide to collect the official tickets (only 5 minutes) and then if busy you can wait for 15 mins to get in. I would advise suncream or a hat as the sun can be quite strong. Once in you go through a security check (just like you would at the airport only faster).
Once inside you get earphones and the tour guide speaks to you directly so it feels like a one on one guide. Our guide was very good starting from the front of the building giving the history of Gaudi and his unfortunate demise. Then progressing into the cathedral (which is nice and cool inside) the tour continues. All in it took 1.5 hrs approx but if you wish to remain after the tour you can do so just be sure to stay within the grounds as once you go out the gate you can't get back in. There is a small museum within the grounds you can visit which is included on the price and beside here you will find toilets and vending machines for soft drinks (only one of them takes notes) the rest need coins.

Our family loved this tour. To start with, the travel agency was professional and organized. Our tour time was 10:00 am and they were punctual. The tour guide was very knowledgeable, friendly and professional. Everything was well explained. I highly recommend this tour to anyone visiting Barcelona.

There was considerable delay despite the claim to fast track, much of this time in full sun. This was partly due to the airport style security. The tour itself was good and explained many features which we would have missed but maybe a good guide book would have been better. In addition our tour was changed the evening before from 8.30 to 12 upsetting all our plans for the day.

The Sagrada Família was truly spectacular, bringing me to tears on entry. It was a delight to have such a knowledgeable guide to walk us through the faces, spires, and architecture on our first visit to the basilica. Our tour left within 10 min of ‘start time’, security was straightforward, and Helena spent at least 15 minutes more than advertised/promised - with the clock starting after security, unlike implied by previous disgruntled reviewers. No complaints at all.

Huge crowds so fast rack
Worth it. Logistics went smoothly... about 16 people for tour in English. Guide was informative, answered questions, fast paced, appeared a bit tired and detached... maybe too many tours that week. Tour was over in less than 60 min. NOT 90 as promised. Better than recorded audio tour .. yes, but at pace of bored guide, not yours. Check the condition of guide by asking questions and studying answers and English speech capabilities before leaving the tour office.

Our tour started at 4 and we didn’t get into the Cathedral til nearly 5. So much for “skip the line.” We had a very large group and the guide was not loud and had a strong accent, so I couldn’t understand a word before we got the audio guides and not much after. He wasn’t particularly friendly or helpful so I think I may have gotten more out of my visit if I just bought an advance ticket and got the audio guide provided by the basilica.

Tour was to start at 9. We showed up at Julia Travel at 8:45 waited till all the groups were divided up and we were assigned a guide and walked over to the entrance to Sagrada Familia, about a 5 minute walk. By this time it was 9:15 and the line for the tour guides to get tickets was at least 15 minutes long so our guide said he'd talk to us about the outside of the building, which was every tiny detail of every statue covering the entrance. No one could follow what statue was where and unless you know a lot about the Bible and the stories, you wouldn't know who he was talking about. After 15-20 minute of this it became obvious that the guide line wasn't every going to get any shorter so our guide went and stood in line and we waited in the wind and cold for 20 minutes for him to get the tickets. Then we waited at the entrance while each tour group was given the time to enter. Thousands of people were there already and we finally got in after 10am, a full hour later than we thought we would be inside. At that point the guide gave us a rushed tour of the inside and told us we were welcome to stay as long as we wanted. So much for the Fast Track tour!! What a joke. We were a group of 6 and all very unhappy with this tour. We would have been better off buying single tickets on our own and getting there early and just doing it on our own.

While visiting La Sagrada Familia is an amazing experience, find a better tour guide option, or just rent the hand held devices. Starting at the beginning, the meeting place for their tours is at the offices of Julia Travel, adjacent to the cathedral. There is one rest room in the tour office, which was out of toilet paper when we got there at 9:45. When I asked one of the attendants to replenish the TP, she just shrugged and said the bathroom maintenance people hadn’t been there yet, and did not offer any assistance. Very inconsiderate, since it can be expected that people would want to use the rest room before they went on the walking tour.

Second, when we booked the tour, it was advertised as being in English. Instead, half of the group was French speaking and the other half English speaking, so the guide had to repeat everything in both French and English. So, the time that he had to talk to us about the church was cut in half, because everything had to be repeated in both French and English. Questions from the French speaking tourists were answered in French and not repeated for the English speakers. Very unprofessional.

Third, although the tour is advertised as “Fast Track,” where you can “sail past long lines of tourists,” that is plain misleading. Once we walked the short distance from the tour office to the group entrance to the cathedral, we waited about 45 minutes to be allowed to go inside. Our guide told us the day before he waited for 2 hours to get in. Once inside, it was crowded, but not absolutely packed. We went early because we were told it gets even more crowded later in the day.

Fourth, our guide had on a dark coat, a dark backpack, and was of medium build with dark hair. He did not carry any kind of talisman or wear a distinguishing color so we could easily find and follow him. When he was done with his explanation in one area of the church, he would just take off for the next stop, and left it up to us to find him in a sea of people that looked just like him. I asked him why he was zooming through the church so quickly, and he said he had another tour due to start in 15 minutes, so he had to get this one done and get back to the office.

We have had many guides before, both on private and small group tours, and this was the worst guide I think we have ever had. Despite waiting around to go in for 45 minutes, he didn’t engage with us, ask us questions or give us background information about Barcelona, the cathedral or interesting factoids to pass the time. Once we gained admission, he just repeated his explanations by rote. He had no underlying knowledge of the cathedral other than the script he had memorized for the tour. Some of the information he provided about the apostles was wrong, but that was probably due to errors in the script he was given to memorize.

So, don’t miss La Sagrada Familia, but find a different tour company or do it with the hand held devices. It’s unfortunate that such a shoddy tour company and guide can diminish a truly spectacular work of art.

I usually take tours for one of two reasons: 1) convenience and saving time at the entrance; 2) quality of the info and local character of the tour guide. I got none with Pedro from the Julia Tour Sagrada Familia. Such a disappointment! We come off season and spend 40 minutes out of 1.5hr tour at the entrance, waiting for Pedro to get the tickets and get in, all while walk-ins waved us from the inside. No line. That “killed” my reason#1. While inside I was expecting to get something worthwhile the wait from Pedro. That killed my reason #2. What a bland, disengaged, primitive presentation?! Oh and did I mentioned the size of the group? 30 people at the “dead” season. In 10 min we split from the group and decided not to waist any more time. That was a good choice, because Sagrada Familia is breathtaking, not like anything else. Leave enough time not to be rushed and explore it at your own path. Don’t forget to stop at the museum to learn about this masterpiece, because Julia’s tour is useless. Actually, total rip-off.
They picked us up at the hotel - a group of five - took us to the Sagrada skipping the lines and then took us to our cruise ship. Excellent english.
I visited the magnificent church but could not enter due to restrictions. A must watch place. Entry tickets are available in their website. advance booking required.

wow blown away by the whole place. You do much better with a guide and our guy Jamie was good.We took the English only tour and at first i was worried that we would not be able to hear but when you get inside you have an ear piece and he has a microphone so all good.The outside is amazing but the colours inside and the scale of the place, just wow.Its good to see that they are definitely still working on it , blocks of stone on cranes whizzing about, also the bits that have been finished in the last 8 months that aren't in any of the post cards.
There wasnt a queue to get in when we went at mid day ,only the queue for the group entrance, so much for the ticket to beat the queues !!!

Our tour was on a Tuesday at 4:00 pm. Our group was 15-20 people, and between them and the city streets, we couldn’t hear our tour guide. We tried moving right up to him, but still, we struggled.

Our main issue, was that we paid to skip the line. We didn’t get to skip a line. We were corralled into a large group waiting pen (with literally 100 other people) and they took us in a group at a time. What was infuriating...was that large groups arrived well after us, and were let in ahead of us. In total, we waited 25-30 minutes in the pen, before we were allowed to enter.
