Our tour started and ended on time. Our guide was well versed in both the approved tour script and also his own knowledge of the cathedral, Gaudi, neighborhood, and political context. He was responsive to other tour guests and was easy to follow. We would certainly take another tour with him.

A visit here is a must when visiting Barcelona. However, skipping the line and having a guide are well worth the money. This is because the place gets very busy and long queues form. Also, the guide shows you lots of things you would probably miss on your own. Would definitely recommend.

The quality of the sound of the audio system was average. Both my husband and I had sets of which the one earphone didn't work at all. It took some time for the tour to get going as a couple of sets of other tourists had to be replaced completely.
Well worth a visit, stunning. Had to queue for a bit, but nothing like others that got tickets on the day. Pre book tickets is a must.
Pedro was a great guide. Very enthusiastic and knowledgeable. The audio system worked well, and The Basilica was Magnificent!
We went on the tour at 16::00, and it was an amazing experience given the late afternoon sun beaming into the west side of the interior. Great tour, and an amazing place.

The cathedral is a must see in Barcelona. It’s necessary to get tickets in advance if you wish to visit. I ordered the fast track tour after I was unable to find tickets on the cathedrals website With the huge crowds and the security screening we had to wait an hour to enter. However, this gave us tine for more pics. Without a tour guide or a audio guide you will miss much. Awesome, creative architecture and beautiful stained windows. Gaudi’s vision is amazing Our guide was very good
Booking the tour was easy . We were taken at the appointed time across to the Sagrada Familia. The guide was so informative and the church was a wonder, just amazing.

This was a very good deal for the price. I will say it was a hot day, not there fault and it was during the end of the busy season so lots of people. It would be helpful to know that the ticket needed to be redeemed at your center (which if it stated I did not read carefully enough), In the end it was well worth the price and less than I would have paid thru the cruise line.

Our guide was funny and very informative was a great tour all round booing the tour in advance was a good move because there were so many tourists some of them had to have missed out on a wonderful landmark

Sagrada Familia is strange, quirky, and beautiful in its own eclectic way. Definitely worthwhile, inside and out. Best in spring and fall; long waits outdoors. We visited on the 2nd of September and it was uncomfortable in the sun. I would avoid July and August. Tour helps to shorten the wait and the guide was fine & a devoted enthusiast. His English was excellent. Museum models are fascinating. I came away wishing that Gaudi had completed the project in the 20s. The newer construction lacks whimsy and complex craftsmanship of the early sections. Still—it's wacky and wonderful.

Sagrada Familia is just an absolute awe-inspiring piece of architecture. Antoni Gaudi has such a unique perspective approach to his work. Our guide was Jordi, and he really has a passion for this tour. He really explained not just how Gaudi did what he did but also the why behind it. He was very easy to understand and had a very pleasant approach to his tour. Highly recommend him AND the tour WOW!!!

This was a very informative tour. Our guide Anke was quite knowledgeable and shared her expertise about the history of La Sagrada and it’s many architects including the infamous and original genius behind this stunning cathedral- Gaudi. We met at the ticket office across the street from La Sagrada Familia and walked easily to the sight with our group of 25. We skipped the long lines and entered through security easily. Headphones were distributed to all and were very clear and easy to use. Anke gave us detailed info about both the inside and outside without ever getting long or boring! Quite a wonderful tour that was just the right length and booking through trip advisor ahead of time gave us the date and time we wanted at a great discount over the walk in price. Highly recommend!

Wonderful tour. Very knowledgeable guide. Crowded but able to follow guide easily. Would definitely recommend this tour, as pre-purchasing tickets avoided the multiple long lines at each entrance. Meeting location was easy to find. Staff respected our tour time and we were promptly placed into groups. We toured during the busy afternoon hours and were very impressed with our ability to not feel rushed.

Sagrada Familia is one solid reason to come to Barcelona. National Catalan pride keeps this a gigantic beauty a celebration of the senses.Determination to complete this work has taken it 137 years from beginning idea to a building permit finally issued in August of 2019. Exciting blend of nature so elevated that it forms the center of the theme of God’s success, and man’s enterprise by an eccentric long dead, but very much alive genius, Gaudi. The tour was done by an articulate your woman named Marta, and it was informative, thorough, and interesting. Worth the time and the cost.

I absolutely loved seeing and experiencing Sagrada Familia, however, I do feel you can do this without a guided tour. You have to wait for about half an hour before being taken to the Sagrada, then queue for about 20mins for going through security. The guide was very good but wasn't telling you anything you couldn't see and understand yourself. I would recommend just queue and go in yourself - think it would even be quicker and cheaper that way.
I liked our tour guide! He was very thorough and took his time at every stop he made during the tour.

We could have used better instructions as to where to meet our tour. We thought we were getting our tickets at the cathedral and didn’t realize that we had to go to a private tour office so it took us a while to figure out where to go.

One can not overlook a visit to this stunning, architectural beauty. We traditionally like out-of-the norm places, but this cliché visit in Barcelona is A MUST. Highly recommend this visit with a tour guide to get the best knowledge of the beauty that you’re beholding.

The famous place is a must-see, absolutely breath-taking view right when you exit from the met station!
Tour itself was okay, at the start our tour guide wasn't very clear (we were in a pretty large group and it was hard to gather around) but once we were inside the temple, we were given a pair of headphones and receiver which was rather helpful.

Our guide was only with us for 1 hour to explain the statues outside the temple, the pillars and imagery inside, then we were free to explore any other places on your own, which made the trip more personal. Other areas included the place around the back where as a large group we weren't allowed to go to during the guided tour as it's meant to be a quiet space for meditation and prayer.

This is the third time in 20 years I have visited this site and it it truly stunning and one of my favourite places ever. The architecture is so incredible and it is amazing to see the progress and changes that happen between each visit. Definitely book before you arrive and the tour helped facilitate a very busy attraction.

Our tour was absolutely fantastic, beaten only by the breathtaking views inside and outside of the La Sagrada Familia. Our tour guide was excellent with great knowledge regarding the La Sagrada Familia, spoke using excellent English, and was happy to answer any questions we had! Would 100% recommend this trip to any others.

Julia Travel seems very efficient and organised. Am not really sure I would recommend having a tour guide though, as personally I just like to wander around. But some interesting info on the tour, and they get you through all the security process a little more quickly and easily. Also, they do leave you inside at the end, so you can wander around then.

We had the tour with the option for the towers, but lifts were not working, got a refund.

The building itself is overall well worth visiting, as it is a pretty unique bizarre monstrosity. The interior is fairly dull though. A good metaphor perhaps of the whole concept...

Easy to find Julia Travel. I saw another review that said it was hard to find. It was right where they said to go, across the street from Sagrada Familia. The tour started right on time. No lines to wait in. The information provided was good. It is a one and a half hour tour with a headset provided so you can hear the guide. There were about twenty of us in our group.
The guide was informative and he knows his stuff. Very friendly and I can’t diss the tour but everyone in our group said it was okay and not the best one they have been on.
This adventure was just all around an amazing time! Horse back riding was my favorite! The guides are fantastic and the people you meet are awesome and from all over!! Great value as well!
The tour was very informative. We had a large group and still moved through the cathedral with ease. Beautiful!
Tour and tour guide excellent. Weather was very hot so it was great to miss all the long queues. Very enjoyable afternoon.

Out tour guide was superb. Her name is Anke and she is originally from Germany, but living for more than 16 years n Barcelona. Very insightful, very patient and with a lot of passion for the topic of Antonio Gaudi and the Sagrada Familia. Amazing memory. Hope to have her as a tour guide after 2026, when the church is finished, again.
Really enjoyable tour our guide Albert was knowledgeable and had a great sense of humour. Loads of people milling around entry was organised chaos with so many people but all worked well.
Guide was excellent, enjoyed it. Busy place, a bit of waiting around at the start of the tour. Headsets were good.
Our guide led us through the story of Sagrada Familia, explaining the symbolism and artistry of this uniquely beautiful sacred place, as Gaudi meant the story to be told.

The tour was awesome. Our tour guide did an awesome job. The tour itself took me back to a time of reflection. It was needed. It was amazing. I do believe more people need to take advantage of this tour.

I am a person who sees and hears things from a deeper perspective. That tour open my mind to a lot of strides that we as a nation are and need to make. The tour also allowed me to see that we are and were never alone. Together we can definitely accomplish the task.

Looking forward to seeing it with the next addition.

We were initially very enthusiastic about joining such a unique guided tour. However our guide was behaving rather like an actress instead of focusing on giving us useful and interesting information. After every third sentence she was asking if we understand her and nobody obviously dared to say that her accent was very Spanish and difficult to understand. Secondly her multiple jokes about her boyfriend's name Josef etc were misplaced and not interesting at all... she has spent perhaps 25-35 % of the time of blank speaking. What's more, at the beginning of the tour in the cathedral. she was called to go back to the office to pick up late arrived participants of the tour. Thus, some people who have arrived on time had to leave earlier the tour because we were late with the schedule. it is a pity such a chef oeuvre of Gaudi was so badly presented to us for such a high price. The guide name was Isabelle, i recommend to avoid her if possible.

The Sagrada Familia is an amazing building as it stands but being on a guided tour with an incredibly knowledgeable tour guide just bought it all to life.

Alex, our guide, was full of snippets of information not only about the building but also about the man himself, Gaudi.

After the tour we felt that we almost knew the man personally which made understanding his work much much easier.

If you can afford the extra cost to get a tour guided vist around this incredable monument to cutting edge architecture i would recommend it very highly

We did this with Carlos from Julia Travel. He is extremely knowledgeable and explains various parts of the Basilica you would never understand on your own! The trip was well organized and he got us in quickly!
This Basilica is one of the most amazing things I have ever seen and Carlos made it even more spectacular with his knowledge that he shares in a most enjoyable way.
I highly recommend this trip.
Take note the lines for Sagrada were very long every time we went near.

We had just a day and a half in Barcelona before cruising so we wanted to be efficient. The hop on-hop off bus stops right there. the tour office is tucked a bit out of the way but anyone will point you to the place. Our group was right-sized, the tour guide knowledgeable and pleasant. The length of the tour was just right. We went early in the morning which I think is wise.
Great tour! Our guide was informative and entertaining. Tickets sell out, so it’s important to plan ahead.
We enjoyed this tour greatly. Our guide was informative and passionate about the Sagrada, two qualities I greatly appreciated.
Great tour and very educational. Felt like the value of the experience was great and would recommend, especially if you have limited time in Barcelona.

Excellent tour of a stunning building by an extremely knowledgeable and entertaining tour guide, Isabel. Well organised & punctual. My 17 and 14 year old daughters and I thoroughly enjoyed it and will be back to see it all finished in 2026. Highly recommended.

Really enjoyed our 2 hour tour of the Basileia. Guide was a local and both educated and entertained us. Group was about 16 of us

Highly recommend as it was a good value.

Despite being in a group tour and despite the fact that Sagrada Familia was packed with tourists, we felt that we still managed to learn the essential basics about Sagrada Familia from our tour guide. The headphones worked well, and our guide spoke clear and good English. We did have to wait for a little while as our guide sorted out the group entry, but once were entered the attraction, everything went smoothly. While you cannot expect much personal engagement with the guide under a group setting, our guide did invite us to ask questions after she finished introducing each highlight. We can't wait to come back in seven years' time when the construction completes!

Great experience! Beautiful cathedral! Great guide! Well worth the price. The tour last about an hour but make sure not to exit but to go back and enjoy the sanctuary on your own. If you exit you won’t be able to re-enter.

We really enjoyed the tour. The guide is knowledgeable, but does not bore one with too much information. The wireless link is great because one can wander away from the group and still follow the commentary. Incredible building with lots to see!

Get a tour or you will be on s long line trying to get in.
Guide spoke good English and she was very nice

The tour allowed us to skip the line to enter the church. Our guide was very knowledgeable about the architecture of the outside of the church. Once inside, you were able to walk around a bit. Our guide gave us headphones, so that he could speak in english, but whisper so as not to disturb the silence of the church. The overall tour was pretty quick and you could stay as long as you would like inside.
Knowledgeable guide. We didn’t wait long to enter. Amazing and beautiful place. I’d love to go again.

The guide is great, start from outside so we can take whole church photo and listen to it’s history. Very clear for every detail of design and history inside and outside of church. Well knowledgeable tour guide lady.
Very good tour guide. Knowledgeable and organized. Advance purchase through Tri Advisor saved a lot of time and headache.
Glad to experience guided tour. Definitely site to see. Suggest booking days ahead of your visit during high tourist season.

Really good experience with the ticket agency and the tour guide.
The agency is right opposite LaSagrada Familia and staff were friendly and helpful.
I went dressed as advised on agency site for this attraction but I noticed many other people in sandals, above knee garments and strappy tops. Not sure why the advice is on there.!!?
La Sagrada is amazing and worth the money.

We booked the English only tour at 4pm and this turned out to be a great choice. The tour guide was very knowledgeable, spoke very good English, and had insightful stories that he shared with us. Everything was on time. I would definitely recommend the tour.
Beautiful church, must see! Tour guide provided good facts but did not deliver in an engaging manner.
Toured on July 19 with Tanya as our guide. She did a wonderful job, very informative and personable. This is a must see in Barcelona.
We had a great tour with Isabelle. She was passionate about telling us the history of the Sagrada Família and she really made the tour for us.

Excellent way to get into Sagrada Familia, skipping all the long lines. Tour guide was very enjoyable, clearly explaining about the highlights of the church in english through earphones and receiver that all of us in group were given. very worthwhile tour.

This is great way to see this must see sight when you have limited time by skipping the line. Going in late afternoon, 3:00 tour ending at 4:30 allowed us a spectacular view of the stained class windows when the light was low in the sky. The rain prevented more commentary about the outside elements of the architecture. Highlighting some of the displays in the museum would have been nice, but all in all a worthwhile tour.
This is a must see. Spectacular and unique architecture. Unfortunately very crowded when we were there - early afternoon. Luckily we booked in advance.
Great tour, we had a family of 4 visiting, and it was a fantatstic tour! Def use a fast track if you don’t want to wait

This was a very nice tour of Sagrada Familia with Jaime, our knowledgeable and personable tour guide. Tour began right on time from a convenient meeting point across the street from the church. Tour hit all the highlights of the church and was enjoyable.
A "MUST SEE" in Barcelona! Words or my pictures can not capture the beauty! Our guide was wonderful!
If your into Cathedrals or contemporary architecture, this is a must stop. Get tickets in advance - there are long lines just to get tickets, then to get in.

We had a 9am skip the line and tower visit tour. Our guide was lovely but somehow we still had to queue for about 30 minutes to get in. It seemed like we were in the normal group line, rather than a skip the line queue. Maybe it was just because of security, I don’t know for sure.

Once we got in, our guide told us that the towers were closed that day! This was incredibly disappointing as we had paid extra to go up the towers, We wished we had been told earlier so we could have had the option of changing days. We found it hard to believe that the tour operator didn’t know this in advance.

The other disappointing thing was that our tour guide’s microphone wasn’t working properly. We kept telling her we couldn’t hear her, but she said she wasn’t good with technology so couldn’t do anything. So we didn’t hear much commentary,

Luckily the church itself is so amazing that our day wasn’t ruined completely.

This was the highlight of the trip. Booking tickets in advance was very easy, and the audio phone that comes with it was really good and detailed. Once your in there, you have all the time you need. Be aware we saw loads of people getting stuck because they didn't have covered shoulders and some people had to buy overpriced shawls from street vendors.
The cathedral itself is incredible, and if your not going inside you aren't doing it justice.

Excellent guide and a very short wait to enter the church. I was under the impression that we would be going up one of the towers but was told it was not part of tour. Our group was not too large. After the guide was finished you could stay in the church and as long as you wanted to.

Good guide and good value. Very informative and not too large a group.

Would only recommend going to this amazing site without a qualified guide.

The tour of Sagrada Familia was impressive but crowded, Our tour included 30 people so it was difficult to hear the guide. We particularly enjoyed the stained glass windows with the sun light shining through.

La Sagrada de Familia is really worth a visit. The exterior was impressive at first sight, but when our guide shared the story behind each sculpture, Gaudí’s life and the design of the windows that would allow the light in the basilica to change throughout the day, to also reflect the cycles of life, I was completely swept away. The interior was impressive and must be seen. There are no words to describe this impressive piece of art.

The tour brought alive the true genius of Gaudi. One of the most amazing architectural structures in the world. Add the religious significance and the detail in every part of the basilica and you will be entranced.
Having a guided tour and jumping the queue is the way to go. A great experience, very informative and the money is well spent.
Very interesting and our guide was excellent. Highly recommend - especially to skip the lines! It's an amazing structure and the history on it is also extremely interesting.
Seemed like we did the right thing by buying tickets in advance and skipping the lines. I'd recommend bringing your own headphones for the tour!

The tour started from the office which was full and it seemed a bit chaotic-big queue to sign in for various tours but eventually our guide gathered our group up and we walked to the church - it’s a very busy area! We had a short wait while the guide sorted our group admission out - but nothing like the wait if you just turned up to go in - so pre booking is best. The guide was informative and we enjoyed our visit.
Good and interesting tour and tour-guide. We also got to spend time to check out the place on our own after. Really magnificent building.

One of the 'must sees' of any trip to Barcelona. With 4 million visitors last year and likely more than that this year, a pre-booked, fast track ticket is a must. In peak season the queues get so long that the police have to close streets around the Sagrada Familia. Be warned however, even Fast Track is not particularly fast. Our guide kept apologising and saying it didn't normally take so long but we didn't visit in peak season so goodness only knows what it is like queueing in the July/August sunshine. The building itself rates an excellent but the tour started late and just felt rushed and a bit cattle class.

First of all Sagrada Família is a must see when I’m Barcelona. It is definitely a Gaudí masterpiece. The tour guide was very informative. She also engaged the kids in the tour very well She talked about architecture of the place, the phases of construction and Gaudí himself. Recommend this tour

We booked a group (7) ‘skip-the-line, fast track’ tour with Julia Travel. The actual group size was much larger than the 9 max we were promised. However the tour guide was very informative and enthusiastic. Be prepared to wait even if you have one of the above tickets - you still have to wait your turn, along with many other groups. It really is worth the wait - walking into the Familia Sagrada was a ‘wow’ moment. We would like to return when it is complete in 7 years time.

Christine from Julia Tours provided information for an amazing experience that I will never forget. Gaudi was a genius, taking over the construction of a Gothic structure, and converting it to a parabolic structure with nature inspired branches. The light as it moves through the day changes the colors in the apse on each side of the Church. We were not there during a service, but at noon there was a request for silence, and those of us who sat and listened to the singing of Ave Maria as we reflected on our blessings felt joy in the experience.

This was a very convenient way to get into the Cathedral and get a little information about what to see there. The guide tells you about the story of the architect and the construction of the building. Then the museum fills in the rest with lots of photos and detailed information.
Please try to get here very early in the morning before 9:30 a.m, also make sure to go back and visit in the evening
Loved the personalized stories by our tour guide about the La Sagrada Familia. My family of four enjoyed the beautiful church. .
A great historical review of this magnificant site! Our guide pointed out features we would no doubt have missed on our own.

Georgina was a perfect tour guide, She was very engaging & asked some questions at the start so that our small group got to know each other. I was running late for start of tour, but this company said no problem & just rescheduled me to start 45 mins later.
I thoroughly recommend this Tour to anyone.

We enjoyed this amazing church so much. It took long to build up to now and still has 7 years left. Gaudi was so forward thinking in his design. The columns are like trees! The lighting through stain glass windows causes awe. The details of Christ's life in relief are numerous and exquisite. We would visit again because there is so much worth seeing again.

Worth every penny! We arrived 10 min before 10 at the address described in the receipt. It is close to the east facade. We left with our tour guide, and headed to the Sagrada Familia. She gave a great tour in Spanish and English. It took around two hours and went to the museum afterwards. We had a great time with Alexandra. Thank you!

It can definitely be busy and crowded, so it was great to reserve a time and ticket in advance. We just walked up at our time, went through security and then were free to wander the church. We didn't get a tour but walked around and enjoyed all the space had to offer. I recommend the stop if you are there!

It's a very beautiful and interesting church. However, it's very different from old traditional churches. Because it's so modern and busy, you even do not feel like in church. But it's definitely worth visiting!
We had a bi-lingual tour from Julia Tours. The older gentleman was excellent switching languages and including everyone. He provided good information and was just the right length. Very good.

We booked this skip the line tour through our travel agent in New Zealand and.... SO glad we did. The guide was a lovely young Spanish, English speaking art student, whose knowledge of Gaudi's work and his visions for the cathedral simply made the whole experience fantastic. She explained the colours of the windows, the structure of the tree shaped columns and the baffling difference in styles on the exterior. If you want to visit the cathedral... and please do!!!!! make sure you book a guided tour. It will make all the difference.

This tour was fantastic- our tour guide Isaac was perfect. We lucked out and booked the tour last minute when the regular tickets were sold out. It turned out this tour was so much better than using the audio guide. Highly recommend!

This tour primarily gets one into the church ahead of everyone waiting in the long lines. The tour guide was very good and provided us a good background and history of the church with lots of useful insights into its history and function. At the end, we could hang around in the church and its shops and museum as long as we wanted.

The sagrada familua is a barcelona must see. One hundred years in the making and it is almost completed. Beautiful architecture. All four facades are gorgeous. If you don't get priority access be prepared to wait in line. Loved this site.

After some difficulty locating the tour office to start the tour, having a local guide who obviously had a passion for the architecture and a wide knowledge of the background to its construction, made for an enjoyable and informative tour.

Be sure to book a tour to the Sagrada Familia before going as it became clear everything was sold out when we arrived. Luckily I had seen this before travelling and booked with this tour. The Meeting point is very near by and easy to spot - right in the midst of the square. Our tour guide was an older man who was very knowledgeable about everything to do with the location. We stayed with the guided tour purely because of what he was telling us (which usually I never do because I feel people ramble on and skip over things you may want to see).
Definitely a must book!

Expensive but probably worth the money. We did "skip the lines" and the guide was very good. For a once in a lifetime visit, I always feel it is worth the cost to have a local expert explain the venue.
This was truly the highlight of Barcelona, WOW. Beyond my wildest dreams the shear scale and beauty of this piece of history that we were a part off.

You have to find the office (which is easy enough to find, about 5 min walk outside the metro L2 station exit) and check in first. Staff is friendly and assigned you as group 1 or 2

It does its job, we don’t have to wait for a long time. Our tour guide gave us a very full-on introduction through the whole journey. Unfortunately maybe he talked too fast or maybe English is not our mother language, we did not catch half of the introduction :( (when we were in Vatican and Pompeii, even with local accent, both our tour guides drew our attention through the whole journey and kept checking if we were all understood)

Also the price DOES NOT include the trip to the tower! So be mindful if you would like to take a look from the tower. Which is quite disappointing.

Next time if we come here again for the tower, will just buy normal ticket from official website and choose the tower section.

After all, this cathedral is an amazing architecture and still under construction.

Very efficient and well paced tour. The guide was excellent at keeping everyone together. She had a small microphone and the guests each had personal earphones attached to a small receiver on a lanyard around the neck which allowed us to not have to stay right next to the guide to hear everything she said. Highly recommend this way to tour this incredible building. A marvelous example of one man's vision and life work which is still under construction over 100 years later.

Sagrada familia is one of the most unique structures I have ever visited and compares to seeing the pyramids, the Taj Mahal or Macchu picchu for the first time.
Our guide was excellent and made the experience even more memorable.

We did not go inside but it is so impressive outside from all sides that you really dot need to go inside. Lots of people all around it. Amazing architecture and a true landmark of Barcelona. You will not regret it.

I do recommend this tour, as you can walk straight past the huge line. But no matter what time of year you visit Barcelona, this visit to the Sagrada Familia will always be a packed house. So expect heaps of people and multiple groups inside and outside this place.
Be sure not to miss this one! The visions and accomplishments of Gaudi are mind boggling. Be sure to visit !

I had heard so much about this church and Gaudi's relationship to it. The inside is amazing to see in the height and different ways the colored glass is impacted by the light in various settings. The continuous building defies logic to me as it is so large and impressive already. There are plans to close off a nearby street and continue building for a number of more years but I don't see the logic in never stopping. No one expects it to be finished when it is predicated to be done.
This is undoubtedly a "must see" in Barcelona. The wide expanse of use of light, various art forms and detail of the "Greatest Story Ever Told" is simply awe inspiring.

I was shocked to see the outside of this church as it is so very different in every way possible! I found it to be odd and not visually pleasing. However, the inside is very different. The continuity and the planning of the interior was wonderful and showed a clear vision. I will say however that perhaps because of it's "difference" and number of visitors the feeling of a place for worship was not there.

Wow, what a wealth of information available through our guide about this overwhelming creation. We learned much about the sculptors and architects that have been and still are active in the completion (eventually) of Sagrada Familia. Really - don't miss this tour and going inside, it's a true marvel!!!!!

There is so much background info you’d miss out on if you visited without a guide. It was very helpful to have someone to walk us through the sculptures and Gaudís thinking: the work behind the work. Really recommend this tour to a) get in to SF at all, b) to skip the lines, and c) receive a full, but potted 1-1/2 explanation.
It's not one of the best structures, but it's worth coming to take a visit. Skipping the queue is a plus. Our guide was very knowledgeable, but her accent was sometimes had to understand.

Booked this tour and were so glad we did otherwise you spend a lot of time queuing for tickets. Booked the 12 noon tour and found the meeting point easy enough and tour set off on time...we had mini radios which were essential so be able to hear the guide and they worked well. The entire tour lasted on 1 hour and 10 mins and I felt the guide was very rushed and he was quite grumpy if anyone asked a question. He was Spanish and whilst his english was quite good he spoke fast and some of our group English was their 2nd language so didn't always understand what he said and if asked a question he told them they should have been listening,,,,,,anyway we did learn a lot and this building is totally awesome and what an experience....If going to Barcelona this is a must visit and also go with a guide to get the most out of the experience .

If you want to see the Sagrada Familia, pre-booked tour tickets are the way to go. Otherwise you have to queue, we arrived at 11 45 am for our pre-booked tour at 12 and already the queue was for tickets for 1745 that day. The tour is fabulous, and well worth it,giving a brief but comprehensive history about the building and its content. Local knowledge is much better that any guide book, any day.

The tour was great, having the individual devices for the audio was great. Our guide was very knowledgeable and provided some great insight to this amazing Basilica. We went in late afternoon and having the priority access made a big difference. Highly recommended and a not to miss tour.

have visited sagrada familia in one of my trips to barcelona, such a beautiful place and peaceful inside well worth
it visiting, beautiful place

The tour was excellent. The church is the most amazing cathedral that we have ever seen. The guide was good and very knowledgeable. The only criticism that we have is that he spoke too fast. He acknowledged that before the tour and said since he was Spanish he was used to speaking so fast, but he would slow down. He never did.
A tour not to be missed.

You need to book in advance. the Sagrada Família Tour guarantees your entrance to Gaudí's masterwork. The guided tour will make your visit very beneficial, taking you to the Catalonian art & architecture. and to hear the story of Barcelona's most famous personality

Be sure to take advantage of the priority access. It will save you hours of waiting in line. This cathedral always has thousands of visitors. You should go early in the morning when it first opens because later in the day it becomes very crowded.

I have travelled the world for 40 years think the Sagrada familla is the most incredible experience I have had. Our wonderful guide Vincent was not only informative but also very humorous, with a wonderful quick wit. My wife and I visited this church during our 50th wedding anniversary vacation. Everything about this church is different from other churches we have visited in europe. Most churches are more detailed on the inside than outside. This church is the opposite. Whole stories are told on the outside of this church and even in different styles. The inside is unique because the main architect, Gaudí, embraced nature. So the columns holding up the inside look like trees. And the stain glass is extensive but unlike other churches we have been in. It is monochromatic with the color shifting from blue to green to red as the sun travels across the church from rise to setting.

The church was started in 1882 but is still being completed. Construction is currently expected to be completed in 2026. So there are cranes in place and construction areas in various places. But what has been completed make this church a must see.

Gaudi at its finest.
Gaudi died in 1926 and had spent 12 years on this building. Now more than 90years later it is still not finished but a sight to be hold.
We paid extra and went up the Passion Tower. Don’t do it, if you are scared of heights or for that matter, small spiral staircases that seem to turn forever 🤪
